evidence.claim: Tshisekedi said the 145-territories program was meant to promote territorial economies, improve rural living conditions through massive public investment, reduce rural-urban disparities, and was entering effective implementation with 2,200 projects.
evidence.title: 9eme conférence des gouverneurs: le président Tshisekedi se félicite de la stabilité des institutions provinciales et fait la promotion du "pdl 145 T".
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi said the 145-territories program was meant to promote territorial economies, improve rural living conditions through massive public investment, reduce rural-urban disparities, and was entering effective implementation with 2,200 projects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential statement with detailed program intent and implementation framing, but still self-reporting.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi because he articulated the program and claimed ownership of its implementation.
contrary_evidence: The same article records complaints from governors about low own-revenue collection, weak transfers, and lack of provincial investment.

evidence.claim: The prime minister said the government deposited the 2023 budget on time, valued at $14.6 billion, about 32 percent above the previous year, and said it would accelerate the 145-territories development program championed by President Tshisekedi.
evidence.title: Dans le respect du délai constitutionnel, le Premier Ministre Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde a déposé à l’Assemblée nationale le Projet de Budget pour l’exercice 2023 chiffré à 14,6 milliards de dollars américains
evidence.excerpt: The prime minister said the government deposited the 2023 budget on time, valued at $14.6 billion, about 32 percent above the previous year, and said it would accelerate the 145-territories development program championed by President Tshisekedi.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official government communication with a concrete budget figure and explicit link to the president’s development program, though the page was only accessible as a search result snippet in this session.
evidence.period_fit: A 2022 government action about the next budget cycle, within the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Tshisekedi through his government and the program it explicitly tied to him.
contrary_evidence: This is a budget proposal and announcement, not a completed spending outcome.

evidence.claim: The CPF for 2022-2026 places strong emphasis on human development and improved access and quality of basic services, alongside governance and stabilization.
evidence.title: World Bank Deepens Commitment to Building Human Capital and Inclusive Development in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The CPF for 2022-2026 places strong emphasis on human development and improved access and quality of basic services, alongside governance and stabilization.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 World Bank release with concrete policy priorities and target-period fit.
evidence.period_fit: Directly 2022 and squarely within the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Tshisekedi-era policy direction, but the program is jointly designed and not proof of full delivery in 2022.
contrary_evidence: This is program design, not completed outcome evidence.

evidence.claim: The CPF rebalances financing toward education and social protection, including girls' learning, women's empowerment, second-chance education, sexual and reproductive health education, and GBV support.
evidence.title: World Bank Deepens Commitment to Building Human Capital and Inclusive Development in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The CPF rebalances financing toward education and social protection, including girls' learning, women's empowerment, second-chance education, sexual and reproductive health education, and GBV support.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific vulnerable-group targeting is explicit and contemporaneous.
evidence.period_fit: 2022 CPF framing, directly relevant to target-period priorities.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Tshisekedi-era policy agenda, though delivery is shared with the Bank and local implementers.
contrary_evidence: The release still describes a fragile, conflict-affected environment, so equitable reach is uncertain.

evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $250 million development policy operation and a $500 million transport/connectivity project, and said the DRC had its first IDA-financed budget support operation since 2005.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $750 Million to Support Critical Governance Reforms, Transport Infrastructure, and Digital Connectivity in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank approved a $250 million development policy operation and a $500 million transport/connectivity project, and said the DRC had its first IDA-financed budget support operation since 2005.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct approval notice with exact financing amounts and clear policy purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Tshisekedi-era reform capacity, but the money and execution are shared with external partners.
contrary_evidence: Approval is not the same as completed delivery or broad welfare impact.

evidence.claim: The transport/connectivity project will finance 440 kilometers of climate-resilient roads in Kasai and North Kivu and lay fiber optic infrastructure along the project roads, with measures to mitigate gender-based violence and manage grievances.
evidence.title: World Bank Approves $750 Million to Support Critical Governance Reforms, Transport Infrastructure, and Digital Connectivity in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The transport/connectivity project will finance 440 kilometers of climate-resilient roads in Kasai and North Kivu and lay fiber optic infrastructure along the project roads, with measures to mitigate gender-based violence and manage grievances.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Concrete infrastructure scope and safeguards are spelled out in the release.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly relevant to social-access infrastructure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the government development agenda, but implementation is donor-financed and shared.
contrary_evidence: Infrastructure approval does not itself show year-end completion or equitable access.

evidence.claim: The report says poverty reduction remained elusive and growth benefits were not broadly shared, while the DRC faced a stark digital divide and major geographic and socio-economic disparities in access.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The report says poverty reduction remained elusive and growth benefits were not broadly shared, while the DRC faced a stark digital divide and major geographic and socio-economic disparities in access.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct development-bank assessment with clear distributional caveats and target-year fit.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly an outcome/context source, limiting how much welfare credit can be assigned to the ruler.
contrary_evidence: Strong macro growth coexisted with weak household-level gains.

evidence.claim: The report says the government liberalized the telecom sector through a new Telecommunications Law with a modern regulatory environment and a universal-access goal.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of Congo Economic Update: Harnessing Growth Through Digital Connectivity to Create Jobs and Reduce Poverty
evidence.excerpt: The report says the government liberalized the telecom sector through a new Telecommunications Law with a modern regulatory environment and a universal-access goal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct policy description from a major multilateral institution.
evidence.period_fit: Within 2022 and directly tied to government policy choices.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the government, but the release does not establish the depth of implementation by year-end.
contrary_evidence: The same report emphasizes a persistent digital divide and unequal access.

evidence.claim: WHO says DRC faced multiple communicable-disease outbreaks in 2022 and that vaccine responses vaccinated 2,635,401 people against cholera, 162,518 against meningitis, and 1,180,268 children against measles.
evidence.title: WHO Global Health Emergency Appeal: DRC
evidence.excerpt: WHO says DRC faced multiple communicable-disease outbreaks in 2022 and that vaccine responses vaccinated 2,635,401 people against cholera, 162,518 against meningitis, and 1,180,268 children against measles.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO emergency publication with explicit outbreak and response numbers.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows crisis-response work under the government's watch, but the operational delivery is largely shared with WHO and partners.
contrary_evidence: The same source shows a heavy disease burden, so response did not eliminate the underlying crisis.

evidence.claim: The government launched a COVID-19 acceleration plan for April-June 2022 aimed at vaccinating at least 11 million people, while official data showed only 890,363 first doses had been given by early April.
evidence.title: Vaccinodromes, equipes mobiles: la RDC accelere sa campagne de vaccination contre la COVID-19 ciblant 11 millions de personnes entre avril et juin 2022
evidence.excerpt: The government launched a COVID-19 acceleration plan for April-June 2022 aimed at vaccinating at least 11 million people, while official data showed only 890,363 first doses had been given by early April.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO regional report with official campaign figures and a concrete target.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This reflects a government-backed campaign, though actual rollout was heavily partner-supported and initial coverage remained very low.
contrary_evidence: Low baseline coverage shows how limited the reach was at the start of the campaign.

evidence.claim: WHO and local health teams used provincial triangulation of vaccine data to improve routine immunization estimates, data quality, and program planning, and the work reported official 2009-2021 triangulated coverage estimates.
evidence.title: De meilleures estimations de couverture vaccinale grace au renforcement des capacites locales sur la triangulation des donnees en RDC
evidence.excerpt: WHO and local health teams used provincial triangulation of vaccine data to improve routine immunization estimates, data quality, and program planning, and the work reported official 2009-2021 triangulated coverage estimates.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct explanation of the measurement process, data gaps, and institutional correction effort.
evidence.period_fit: Directly 2022 and relevant to the year’s service-delivery management.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This supports institutional correction under the health ministry, but it is not a personal presidential action.
contrary_evidence: The source also highlights major data and coverage gaps, so it is not a clean success story.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said about 200,000 IDPs had fled since late March 2022, warned of cholera risk from clean-water shortages, and continued WASH, health, nutrition, and education assistance for the most vulnerable.
evidence.title: UNICEF: Mass displacements in eastern DRC pose a deadly threat to children and young people
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said about 200,000 IDPs had fled since late March 2022, warned of cholera risk from clean-water shortages, and continued WASH, health, nutrition, and education assistance for the most vulnerable.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 UNICEF emergency report with concrete displacement and service-response detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The crisis reflects conditions under the administration's watch, but the service response is largely UNICEF-led and partner-delivered.
contrary_evidence: The source emphasizes that lives remained in grave danger and aid needs were still rising.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said over 2,000 schools had closed since January 2022 because of insecurity and displacement, and that UNICEF and partners had built 428 temporary learning spaces while only 2 percent of education-funding needs were pledged.
evidence.title: The dilemma of schools that shelter DRC’s displaced families
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said over 2,000 schools had closed since January 2022 because of insecurity and displacement, and that UNICEF and partners had built 428 temporary learning spaces while only 2 percent of education-funding needs were pledged.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Retrospective but specific, with direct education-disruption and response figures tied to the 2022 crisis period.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospective on January 2022 onward, so it fits the target period strongly.
evidence.ruler_attribution: The schooling disruption is mostly conflict-driven, but the state's capacity to protect education and reopen schools remains relevant.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF also documents temporary learning spaces and advocacy, so the picture is not pure abandonment.

unresolved_gaps: No direct evidence of nuclear command-and-control, custody, accident-prevention, or safety-safeguard performance under Tshisekedi.
Independent compliance evidence for the Nairobi and Luanda processes remains thin.
Direct command-responsibility evidence and remedy follow-up for police and military abuses are still weak.
Direct evidence on institutional strengthening, political equality, and election-body independence is thin.
Independent 2022 implementation and household-level outcome evidence is still thin.
Direct ruler-attributable outcome data on health, education, nutrition, and protection remains sparse.
Direct evidence of Tshisekedi's own assets, family/business interests, campaign finance, and false statements is missing.
Completed outputs and adaptation under failure are not well documented for the major 2022 programs.
